nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift, splice and missense variants on both MAN1B1 alleles. The two recurrent missense alleles, p.Arg334Cys (an active-site pocket residue) and p.Glu397Lys, sit at conserved residues; in recombinant expression the founding alleles either reduced catalytic turnover about 1300-fold or prevented stable protein expression. In patient fibroblasts the steady-state MAN1B1 protein is extremely low, including for missense alleles with normal or raised mRNA, so most alleles act by destabilising the protein as well as or instead of inactivating it.

nodes.description: Slowed mannose trimming lets incompletely trimmed glycans proceed through the Golgi, where they are converted into hybrid-type structures. Sialylated and fucosylated hybrid glycans such as NeuAc1Hex6HexNAc3 accumulate on serum glycoproteins, including transferrin (at the Asn432 site), IgG and alpha-1-antitrypsin, though in total serum they are often present only in trace amounts. The missing sialic acid on transferrin glycans is what shows as the type 2 isoelectric focusing pattern.

nodes.description: MAN1B1 is expressed mainly in dorsal progenitors and intermediate excitatory neurons of the developing human cortex. Knocking Man1b1 down in cultured mouse excitatory neurons impairs axon growth, dendrite formation and spine maturation. Knocking it down in the embryonic mouse cortex by in utero electroporation increases the proportion of proliferating progenitors while fewer of them exit the cell cycle, and fewer newborn neurons reach the cortical plate. The abstract summarises the progenitor result as impaired proliferation and differentiation; the results section reports increased proliferation with reduced cell-cycle exit, and this node follows the results. This is the only experimental account of how the deficiency affects the brain; it comes from knockdown in mouse rather than from patient tissue, and no patient brain pathology has been described.

nodes.description: Mannose trimming by MAN1B1 is the step that marks terminally misfolded glycoproteins for ER-associated degradation (ERAD), and the enzyme also supports degradation of misfolded alpha-1-antitrypsin through a catalysis-independent route that depends on its cytoplasmic tail. The ERAD role is well established in cell lines; in patient cells it is inferred from the enzyme deficiency rather than measured with a degradation assay. Where the enzyme acts is contested: it has been placed in the Golgi, where it would retrieve escaped misfolded proteins to the ER, and alternatively in ER-derived quality-control vesicles, with the Golgi pattern attributed to an immunofluorescence fixation artefact.

nodes.description: MAN1B1 is a type II membrane glycosyl hydrolase family 47 enzyme that cleaves a single alpha-1,2-mannose from the middle branch of Man9GlcNAc2 to give the Man8GlcNAc2 isomer B. Lymphocyte microsomes from patients show negligible activity of this kind, and patient fibroblasts process Man9 to Man8 at roughly a third of the control rate. The residual trimming is attributed to other ER and Golgi alpha-mannosidases, including the EDEM proteins.
